title: Primary torsion cases for a prime-annihilated sheaf
statement: For a commutative coefficient ring Λ, a scheme X and a prime r, let F be an etale sheaf of Λ-modules with r id_F = 0. Then F is r-primary [def-weil-pbc-primary-torsion]. For any prime p different from r, if F is p-primary, F is a zero object.

source.place: Tag 0GJA (lemma-restrict-to-open), proof: the finite stalk product, five-term exact sequence, and remarks (a) and (b)

proof.text: Apply each additive geometric stalk functor to r id_F = 0. Every stalk element is killed by r, so exponent one proves r-primary torsion.
If p differs from r, r and p^n are coprime. nsmul_eq_zero_iff_of_coprime shows that each p-primary stalk element is zero.
Use sheafHom_ext_of_sheafFiber_map_algClosurePoint from the geometric-stalk conservativity module to identify the identity of F with zero. IsZero.iff_id_eq_zero concludes.

mathlib_searches.query: For a constructible sheaf on a curve, extension by zero across a dense open preserves finiteness of all cohomology groups. A prime-annihilated sheaf is primary for that prime and is zero if primary for another prime or if its annihilator is noninvertible but it has invertible-order torsion.
